newsitem.title: USA: Scripps sees newsprint prices hurting profit.
newsitem.headline: Scripps sees newsprint prices hurting profit.

text.p: E. W. Scripps Co President and Chief Executive William Burleigh said higher year-over-year newsprint prices will dampen profit growth at its newspaper operation in the second half of this year.

Burleigh also said while the Home & Garden Television unit was developing at a faster rate than expected, it still projected higher losses in the third and fourth quarters than in the first half of the year. It did not elaborate.
The company said total second-quarter operating income increased 22 percent to $38.6 million, or $0.48 per share, from $31.7 million, $0.39.
Burleigh also said the absence of political advertising this fall will leave its stations "scrambling to replace that revenue."

In the second quarter, it said newsprint prices fell 20 percent, partially offset by a 14 percent increase in usage. If newsprint remained at its current price, year-over-year costs would be about flat in the third quarter and increase 15 percent in the fourth quarter.
At Home & Garden Television, revenues more than doubled year-over-year to $13 million, and cash operating losses were $1.4 million, compared with $2.7 million last year.
